scenes.tts: A mouse has no opsin, yet light changes its firing and turning. What did the light change?
scenes.visual: Hook first. A large top-down cartoon mouse fills the frame inside a circular arena. A yellow beam enters the left striatum; a teal badge reads NO OPSIN. A blue firing trace falls while the mouse path curves left. Keep the path drawing forward as the question appears. Mark the trace and path schematic. COLOR MAP for both chapters: yellow = light, gold = opsin-linked manipulation, teal = fluorophore or no opsin, blue = measured outcome, red = unresolved alternative.
scenes.narration: A mouse has no opsin, yet light changes its firing and turning. What did the light change?

scenes.visual: Transform the curved mouse path into the gold underline of the title What Did the Light Change? Keep the yellow beam and teal NO OPSIN badge small in opposite corners.

scenes.tts: In wild-type mice, continuous striatal light suppressed firing and biased turning. Illumination had changed tissue without a light-sensitive construct. A light-on comparison therefore changes at least two things: the intended neural activity and the light itself.
scenes.visual: Rebuild the same large mouse and arena. Split the yellow beam into two animated arrows. One gold arrow points to a labelled Intended activity box; one red arrow points to a labelled Light itself box. Both arrows feed the same blue behaviour gauge, marked schematic, which keeps gently oscillating.
scenes.narration: In wild-type mice, continuous striatal light suppressed firing and biased turning. Illumination had changed tissue without a light-sensitive construct. A light-on comparison therefore changes at least two things: the intended neural activity and the light itself.

scenes.tts: A recording can show that activity and behaviour vary together. A manipulation asks a different question. Driving chosen cells tests whether their activity is sufficient for the measured change. Suppressing them tests whether it is necessary. Each answer belongs only to the tested conditions.
scenes.visual: The arena stretches into a horizontal causal track. A dashed grey Activity goes with behaviour link becomes a solid gold intervention arrow. The gold arrow pushes a blue behaviour meter upward, then a gold brake pulls it downward. Labels SUFFICIENT? and NECESSARY? replace one another, while a small TESTED CONDITIONS bracket remains.
scenes.narration: A recording can show that activity and behaviour vary together. A manipulation asks a different question. Driving chosen cells tests whether their activity is sufficient for the measured change. Suppressing them tests whether it is necessary. Each answer belongs only to the tested conditions.

scenes.tts: To separate the two causes, cross construct with light. Put opsin and fluorophore-only animals in two rows. Put light off and light on in two columns. Now every effect of illumination has a matched place to appear.
scenes.visual: The causal track folds into a frame-filling two-by-two arena board. Gold OPSIN and teal FLUOROPHORE rows slide in; dark LIGHT OFF and yellow LIGHT ON columns sweep across. Four large mouse icons enter their cells. Blue schematic behaviour meters grow beside every mouse.
scenes.narration: To separate the two causes, cross construct with light. Put opsin and fluorophore-only animals in two rows. Put light off and light on in two columns. Now every effect of illumination has a matched place to appear.

scenes.tts: You have compared light on with light off only in opsin animals. Which missing comparison would reveal whether light itself moved the behaviour?
scenes.visual: Dim three cells and enlarge only the opsin light-off and opsin light-on cells. A red question mark grows in the empty fluorophore row. The yellow light bar continues sweeping slowly across both rows.
scenes.narration: You have compared light on with light off only in opsin animals. Which missing comparison would reveal whether light itself moved the behaviour?

scenes.visual: Hold the question on screen. Keep the yellow beam shimmering and the red question mark pulsing once, slowly. No answer appears.

scenes.tts: Give fluorophore-only animals the same light. First measure the light effect in each row. Then compare those two effects. The shared light effect cancels. The remainder is the extra light-linked effect associated with carrying the opsin.
scenes.visual: Restore the full grid. A blue light-effect bracket forms within each row. Copy both brackets to the centre and subtract them. Their shared red segment slides together and vanishes; a gold remainder stays. Label the result EXTRA WITH OPSIN, with a small schematic tag.
scenes.narration: Give fluorophore-only animals the same light. First measure the light effect in each row. Then compare those two effects. The shared light effect cancels. The remainder is the extra light-linked effect associated with carrying the opsin.

scenes.tts: Read the board as two differences, not four separate boxes. Measure the light effect in opsin animals. Measure it again in fluorophore animals. Subtract the second effect from the first. This difference of differences identifies the opsin-linked remainder.
scenes.visual: Keep the same board. A blue arrow measures across the opsin row, then a second measures across the fluorophore row. The arrows stack vertically and the lower one subtracts from the upper. The gold remainder expands to fill the centre while the four boxes recede.
scenes.narration: Read the board as two differences, not four separate boxes. Measure the light effect in opsin animals. Measure it again in fluorophore animals. Subtract the second effect from the first. This difference of differences identifies the opsin-linked remainder.

scenes.tts: That remainder is not a license to say the circuit controls the behaviour. Name the cells, the projection, the time window and the assay. Activation tests sufficiency. Silencing tests necessity. Neither says these cells are the only route.
scenes.visual: The gold remainder stretches into a claim sentence frame. Four large slots snap into place: CELLS, PROJECTION, TIME, ASSAY. A gold upward switch docks under SUFFICIENT and a gold brake under NECESSARY. A red ONLY ROUTE stamp approaches, then is pushed outside the safe frame.
scenes.narration: That remainder is not a license to say the circuit controls the behaviour. Name the cells, the projection, the time window and the assay. Activation tests sufficiency. Silencing tests necessity. Neither says these cells are the only route.

scenes.tts: A light spot does not name a pathway by itself. Terminal illumination can also excite labelled axons that only pass through the field. It can drive activity back toward the parent cell bodies. A local receptor block tests whether transmitter action there is required for the measured behavioural effect.
scenes.visual: The PROJECTION slot enlarges into two labelled blocks joined by a gold axon. Yellow light lands on the terminal field. A red arrow runs backward toward the parent block; another red branch bends through the field. A teal receptor-block gate crosses out the local gold synaptic arrow, and the blue behavioural effect disappears while the red alternatives remain visible. Mark the circuit schematic.
scenes.narration: A light spot does not name a pathway by itself. Terminal illumination can also excite labelled axons that only pass through the field. It can drive activity back toward the parent cell bodies. A local receptor block tests whether transmitter action there is required for the measured behavioural effect.

scenes.tts: Finally, verify what the manipulation actually did. Record during and after the light. Confirm expression and fibre placement. Randomize allocation and blind the scoring. Only when the manipulation and its controls work can the matched contrast identify the effect. A claim can be no broader than that contrast.
scenes.visual: The claim frame becomes a large checklist surrounding the same mouse. A moving blue firing trace spans DURING and AFTER. A gold expression patch and fibre tip align over the target. Mouse cards shuffle under RANDOMIZE; an eye icon closes over SCORE. All checks converge on the gold remainder.
scenes.narration: Finally, verify what the manipulation actually did. Record during and after the light. Confirm expression and fibre placement. Randomize allocation and blind the scoring. Only when the manipulation and its controls work can the matched contrast identify the effect. A claim can be no broader than that contrast.

scenes.visual: End card. Collapse the checklist into one gold rule line beside the two-by-two board: A claim can be no broader than that contrast. Hex waves while the yellow light sweeps once across both construct rows.
